summary: Discovery call focused on Atlantic First's compliance and data residency constraints. Customer evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment modes. Key concerns: EU/US residency, logging restrictions for PII, SOC 2/HIPAA evidence, KMS and SSO, and network peering for private control plane. Agreed next steps: send compliance pack, share VPC diagram, schedule technical deep dive.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm maya from redwood inference, we'll keep this to 45 minutes, quick intros?
[00:08] Sara (Atlantic): sara here, head of cloud architecture, we'll be driving the infra questions.
[00:13] Daniel (Atlantic CISO): daniel price, security and compliance, hi.
[00:17] Liam (Redwood SE): hi all, liam o'neill, i'll take the tech deep dive bits.
[00:23] Erin (Atlantic): erin cho, vp digital, mostly product and timeline owner.
[00:28] Tom (Atlantic): tom alvarez, devops, i'll be hands on.
[00:33] Maya: great, objective today is data residency and compliance - high level constraints and if hosted, dedicated or private makes sense, is that right, erin?
[00:40] Erin: yep. timeline is Q4 pilot, decision cadence end of july ideally.
[00:46] Daniel: short version, we cannot have logs containing unredacted pii leave our network for EU citizens, also need HIPAA-compliant flow for some customer support transcripts, and SOC2 posture is required. curious what redwood's options look like.
[01:03] Liam: totally. we support three deployment modes: hosted api (fastest), dedicated reserved capacity (isolated gpu pools but control plane is within redwood), and private (VPC or on-prem with customer-managed control plane). each has different tradeoffs for residency and auditability.
[01:20] Sara: can you clarify the \"hosted\" case - data residency wise? like if we have eu customers, can that stay in eu?
[01:28] Maya: yes, hosted supports region pinning - requests can be routed to eu regions. however audit logs and some meta telemetry may still be centralized unless you choose dedicated with stricter controls or private. we also have a privacy config to limit logging.
[01:43] Daniel: when you say 'some meta telemetry' - what's logged? and can we prevent prompts or transcripts from being logged?
[01:50] Liam: good question. by default we capture request metadata for monitoring (latency, error rates) and a sampling of logs for quality. for enterprise we can disable content logging, and we offer redaction hooks - either client side or server side via regex and pii-masking. in private deployments, logs can be retained only on-prem.
[02:12] Tom: you mentioned redaction hooks - are they real time? we can't have a middle step that sends raw user messages to third-party storage.
[02:19] Liam: yes, you can configure pre-ingest transforms. some customers run a small lambda that strips pii before it hits the inference path; others use our built-in redaction policy. i'll note that automated redaction is not perfect, we recommend a combined approach and strict retention.
[02:33] Erin: HIPAA - do you sign a BAA? and does hosted qualify?
[02:38] Maya: we do sign BAAs for enterprise customers. hosted can be configured for HIPAA workloads with our enterprise plan but many regulated customers prefer Dedicated or Private so that audit logs and control plane visibility meet their infosec requirements.
[02:52] Daniel: what about encryption keys - bring your own key?
[02:56] Liam: KMS integrations are supported. for hosted we support BYOK via customer-managed KMS (we integrate with AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault). for Private on-prem you manage the HSM/KMS fully.
[03:06] Sara: GDPR - we need EU residency and the ability to delete customer data on request. how is deletion handled?
[03:12] Maya: we have per-customer data retention policies with API endpoints to delete data. in hosted, deletion is applied to regionally stored data, and in dedicated/private we can scope retention to your VPC and provide deletion certifications.
[03:26] Tom: network wise for private control plane, do you require a public egress? we need to keep traffic internal.
[03:32] Liam: private control plane can run inside your VPC, peered via AWS PrivateLink or direct connect. no public egress is required for model payloads if you want everything internal; there are options.
[03:43] Erin: great. cost wise how different is Dedicated vs Private?
[03:47] Maya: Dedicated is usually reserved capacity on our infra - predictable monthly commit. Private has a higher upfront and operational fee because of the private control plane and potentially on-prem hardware. we can provide a TCO comparison based on your throughput.
[03:59] Sara: logging restrictions are the sticking point. our compliance team wants to ensure that any PII is never stored in redwood logs even transiently. is there a configurable 'no-log' mode?
[04:09] Liam: yes 
d enterprise customers can enable a strict no-content-logging policy. note that some observability features (per-token cost) rely on some telemetry; we can provide token-level cost attribution without full content by hashing or anonymizing. again, private gives you the most control.
[04:27] Daniel: do you provide audit logs suitable for SOC2 evidence? and can we push them to our SIEM?
[04:34] Maya: yes, we provide structured audit logs and can integrate with your SIEM via syslog/s3/secure-forwarder. for Dedicated/Private customers we can increase retention windows and provide redacted examples for audits.
[04:49] Tom: any limits on model variants in private? we plan to use a couple of open models and maybe a small fine-tuned model.
[04:57] Liam: you can bring models; we support curated open models and customer-tuned artifacts. there are some runtime constraints for very large custom weights on on-prem GPU setups but generally supported.
[05:08] Erin: someone mentioned K V cache earlier in docs - how is that handled if we use private?
[05:13] Liam: the KV cache (sometimes said as kay-vee cache) is ephemeral and lives on the serving nodes. for private deployments, those nodes are inside your network; you control disk encryption and lifecycle.
[05:24] Sara: ok, can you talk through an example flow for an EU customer chat that might contain pii?
[05:29] Liam: flow: client -> pre-ingest redactor in your VPC -> inference node in eu region (hosted or private) -> response; logs streamed to your SIEM or to redwood with content disabled. retention policy applied and deletion endpoint called when needed.
[05:45] Daniel: legal also wants to know about subprocessors and data transfer - will data be transferred to us regions for model serving?
[05:53] Maya: by default we route to the region you select. for hosted we have geo-routing; for Dedicated we pin to specific availability zones; for Private everything stays within your control plane/region. we can provide a subprocessors list in the pack.
[06:05] Erin: what about CI/CD for prompts and evals - can that live in our VPC?
[06:11] Liam: yes, you can run evals on-prem or in your cloud account with the same SDKs. the telemetry can be sent back or kept local.
[06:18] Tom: latency question - private usually adds a little overhead?
[06:22] Liam: there's slight latency differences if you self-host hardware or add network hops for private control plane. Dedicated on our infra with region pinning often hits best latency/cost tradeoff.
[06:31] Sara: any red flags on your side with our timeline (pilot Q4, decision EoJUL)?
[06:36] Maya: tight but doable, we'll need the security questionnaire answers and to run a proof-of-concept (Poc). recommended path: start with Dedicated pilot for 3 months to validate throughput, then if more control required move to Private.
[06:50] Daniel: auditability is key - can we get an example of a redacted audit log and a BAA template?
[06:56] Liam: i'll attach sample logs and the BAA in the pack. note: sample logs will show events, request ids, timestamps, and redaction markers but not raw content.
[07:08] Erin: do you have customers in eu that run entirely in eu regions?
[07:12] Maya: yes, we have several financial customers with EU-only deployments; we can share references under NDA.
[07:19] Tom: how do you handle backups / snapshots - could they contain user content?
[07:24] Liam: we encrypt backups; for private you manage snapshots. for hosted we can configure retention and ensure backups are region-scoped and encrypted with your KMS.
[07:36] Sara: a couple of security details: SSO, role mapping, and least privilege. what's supported?
[07:41] Maya: we support SAML/SSO, SCIM provisioning, and per-user RBAC. roles can be mapped to your IdP groups.
[07:50] Daniel: regarding logging retention policy - our legal wants 90 day default and then option to purge. can that be set?
[07:57] Liam: yes, retention windows are configurable for enterprise customers. for hosted it's usually 30/90/365 presets; Dedicated/Private you can customize.
[08:09] Erin: okay can we try to capture the immediate blockers?
[08:12] Sara: primary blocker: no content leaving EU without redaction.
[08:16] Daniel: second: need BAA and SOC2 report, plus ability to push logs to our SIEM.
[08:21] Tom: third: network - private control plane or private link requirement.
[08:25] Maya: noted. we'll include those in the pack.
[08:29] Liam: quick note on model fallbacks and routing - if you pin to eu and our eu pool is constrained we can fallback to a compatible variant but we can disable automatic fallback for compliance-critical flows.
[08:42] Erin: good to know.
[08:44] Maya: any questions about pricing or commitments now or should we follow up after the pack?
[08:50] Erin: send the pack first and a ballpark for Dedicated.
[08:54] Sara: also include sample SLA language for latency and availability.
[08:58] Maya: will do.
[09:00] Daniel: last question - for HIPAA, if we sign a BAA, any special config needed?
[09:06] Liam: usually we enable stricter logging controls, increase retention and exportability of audit logs, and recommend Dedicated or Private. we'll lay out a checklist in the pack.
[09:18] Maya: recap: we'll send the compliance/security pack (SOC2/HIPAA/ subprocessors list), VPC diagram, redaction patterns and sample redacted logs, and ballpark pricing for Dedicated/Private. schedule the deep technical session for week of july 6th.
[09:34] Erin: thanks everyone.
[09:36] Sara: thanks.
[09:37] Tom: thanks.
[09:38] Meeting ended.
